prompt: Write the checks that catch a vowel counter which ignores capitals, one that counts y, and one that dies on null. Complete isCorrect in the starter file, then run the tests.
explanation: All-lowercase fixtures like "hello" are the reason case bugs survive to production: the only check that pins down case handling is one with capitals in it, such as "AEIOU" -> 5. Likewise, y is only interesting because the contract says it is not a vowel, so a string containing y is the only place that rule is observable. null is not just another string -- it is the input where the method must have documented behaviour, and the checker has to pass it deliberately and catch the NullPointerException a careless implementation throws.
hints: Lowercase-only inputs cannot tell the correct counter apart from the case-sensitive one. Add a check using capitals.
The contract says y is not a vowel, so include a word containing y -- "Yellow Sky" should count 2, and "rhythm" should count 0.
Call impl.countVowels(null) and expect 0, with the whole block wrapped in try/catch that returns false, so a NullPointerException is recorded as a failure.
